title: Given a string, find the minimum number of cuts needed so that every resulting piece is a palindrome. Explain how the Palindromic Subsequence pattern combines with a cut dynamic program, the recurrence, the complexity, and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Palindromic Partitioning (Minimum Cuts to Split a String into Palindromes)

s1_definition.profdef: Palindromic Partitioning asks for the minimum number of cuts so that every segment is a palindrome, and it combines the palindrome table from the Palindromic Subsequence pattern with a one dimensional cut dynamic program. We precompute which ranges are palindromes, then compute the fewest cuts up to each position by trying every palindromic suffix ending there. This runs in quadratic time and space.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India breaks a long routing string into the fewest symmetric chunks for a compact storage format, because each symmetric chunk compresses well. The question is the minimum number of breaks so that every chunk reads the same both ways.
s1_definition.oneliner: Fewest cuts up to position i is the best over every palindromic piece ending at i of one plus the cuts before that piece.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Palindromic Partitioning asks for the minimum number of cuts so that every segment is a palindrome, and it combines the palindrome table from the Palindromic Subsequence pattern with a one dimensional cut dynamic program. We precompute which ranges are palindromes, then compute the fewest cuts up to each position by trying every palindromic suffix ending there. This runs in quadratic time and space.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The National Bank of India breaks a long routing string into the fewest symmetric chunks for a compact storage format, because each symmetric chunk compresses well. The question is the minimum number of breaks so that every chunk reads the same both ways.

**One line to remember:** Fewest cuts up to position i is the best over every palindromic piece ending at i of one plus the cuts before that piece.

sections.s2_technical:
First we build the boolean palindrome table so we can ask in constant time whether any range is a palindrome, using the ends-match-and-inner-is-palindrome rule. Then we define cuts up to index i as the minimum cuts needed so that the prefix ending at i splits fully into palindromes. For each i we look back at every start j where the piece from j to i is a palindrome: if that piece starts at zero the whole prefix is one palindrome needing zero cuts, otherwise the cost is one plus the cuts up to j minus one.

The cut recurrence is `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { if (pal[0][i]) cuts[i] = 0; else { cuts[i] = i; for (int j = 1; j <= i; j++) if (pal[j][i]) cuts[i] = Math.min(cuts[i], cuts[j-1] + 1); } }` with the answer `cuts[n-1]`. A concrete check: a string that is already a palindrome needs zero cuts, and a string of all distinct characters needs length minus one cuts. Senior nuance: this is quadratic in time and space, the palindrome table is the reusable Palindromic Subsequence building block, and the cut layer is a classic prefix dynamic program on top of it.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India stores long routing strings in a compact format where each symmetric chunk compresses efficiently, so it wants to split each routing string into the fewest number of symmetric chunks. Trying all splits is exponential. This is exactly how Palindromic Partitioning works: it precomputes the palindrome table with the Palindromic Subsequence pattern and then finds the minimum cuts with a prefix dynamic program.

The code defines a `RoutingSplitService` exposing `minCuts(routing)` returning the minimum cuts. A `Demo` runs it over a sample routing string and logs the cut count.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is the routing string ABACC. We want the fewest cuts so every chunk is a palindrome.

Step 1 — We build the palindrome table. ABA from positions zero to two is a palindrome, and CC from positions three to four is a palindrome, while the whole string is not.

Step 2 — For position zero the single A is a palindrome, so cuts there is zero.

Step 3 — For position two the prefix ABA is a full palindrome, so cuts there is zero.

Step 4 — For position three the prefix ABAC is not a palindrome. The best palindromic piece ending at position three is the single C starting at three, so cuts is one plus cuts at position two which is zero, giving one.

Step 5 — For position four the prefix ABACC is not a palindrome. The palindromic piece CC starts at position three, so cuts is one plus cuts at position two which is zero, giving one. The answer is one cut, splitting into ABA and CC. The output is below.

```
Oct 27, 2026 9:14:40 PM com.bank.routing.service.RoutingSplitService minCuts
INFO: Min palindromic cuts for ABACC = 1
Oct 27, 2026 9:14:40 PM com.bank.routing.RoutingSplitApplication main
INFO: Minimum chunks minus one for routing ABACC is 1
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Palindromic Partitioning is a two-layer problem where the Palindromic Subsequence pattern provides the foundation. I first build a boolean table that tells me in constant time whether any range of the string is a palindrome, using the rule that a range is a palindrome when its ends match and its inner range is a palindrome. That table is the reusable building block.

On top of it I run a prefix dynamic program. I define the minimum cuts for the prefix ending at each position, and for that position I look back at every start where the trailing piece is a palindrome. If a palindromic piece covers the whole prefix the cost is zero cuts, otherwise it is one cut plus the best cuts for the part before that piece. The answer is the value at the last position, and the whole computation is quadratic in time and space.

At the National Bank of India I used this to split long routing strings into the fewest symmetric chunks for a compact storage format, since symmetric chunks compressed efficiently. I precomputed the palindrome table and then ran the minimum-cut prefix dynamic program. Explaining that the palindrome table comes straight from the Palindromic Subsequence pattern, and that the cut layer tries every palindromic suffix to minimise cuts, is what shows an interviewer I can compose the pattern with another dynamic program.
